title: Country history
source: reversing/findings/FINDINGS-history.md; ghidra/project.json CHistoryContainer::LoadKey (0x1FCC10), CCountryHistory::LoadEntry (0x1ECA90), CCountry::LoadKey (0xCCDA0); BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountryHistory.hpp; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md (CCountry's 126 cases); reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md section 6

file.desc: a country's history: one grammar, at the top or postponed to a date

patterns.desc: applied on that date: the block holds the same keys as the top of the file, and is only a way of postponing them (CHistoryContainer::LoadKey)

entries.desc: CCountryHistory::LoadEntry: 33 keys of its own, and names looked up in the technology, category, government position and law databases. A date inside a date block is not a date to it

alignment.desc: the country's place on the diplomacy triangle, `{ x = .. y = .. }` (CAlignmentPosition)

government_in_exile.desc: makes the country a government in exile (CExileStatusChange)

historical_friend.desc: a country it is historically friendly with

leader.desc: a CLeaderChange; what its value is has not been read

officers_ratio.desc: officer ratio, 1.0 being the full complement

oob.desc: an order of battle in history/units/ to load

military_government.desc: sets this occupation policy on that country (COccupationChange); the policies are the blocks of common/occupation_policies.txt

collaboration_government.desc: sets this occupation policy on that country (COccupationChange); the policies are the blocks of common/occupation_policies.txt

full_occupation.desc: sets this occupation policy on that country (COccupationChange); the policies are the blocks of common/occupation_policies.txt

total_exploitation.desc: sets this occupation policy on that country (COccupationChange); the policies are the blocks of common/occupation_policies.txt

civil_war.desc: sets this occupation policy on that country (COccupationChange); the policies are the blocks of common/occupation_policies.txt

soviet_liberation.desc: sets this occupation policy on that country (COccupationChange); the policies are the blocks of common/occupation_policies.txt

patterns.desc: a technology and the level the country has of it (CTechnologyChange)
a theory and the country's skill in it (CCategoryChange)
a practical and the country's experience in it (CCategoryChange)
a government position and the id of the minister who holds it (CMinisterChange)
a law group and the law in force in it (CLawChange)

alignment.desc: a point on the diplomacy triangle. Only the shape the files use is known: a savegame writes CAlignment's `position = { x y }` instead, which is another loader

ideology_shares.desc: ideology = percent, one line per ideology

country_keys.desc: CCountry::LoadKey: everything a country's own loader takes - what a savegame's country block holds, and what an order-of-battle file may hold beside its units. The unit, deployment and construction keys belong to the OOB schema

acting_capital.desc: where the government sits when the capital is lost

effective_neutrality.desc: save state, as a savegame writes it: the loader takes it, but there is no reason to write it by hand

manpower.desc: manpower in the pool; also kept as the starting manpower

graphical_culture.desc: which graphical culture its units are drawn in

history.desc: the country's history, read by CCountryHistory: dates and history keys

alignment.desc: the place on the diplomacy triangle, as CAlignment reads it: `position = { x = .. y = .. }`

organization.desc: party organisation, as a save writes it
